title: This Tiny Swimming Slug Went Almost a Year Without Eating
subject: sea angel

scenes.text: This tiny swimmer went almost a year without a single meal.
It's a sea angel, a shell-less sea slug that flaps two tiny wings. And it eats only one thing.
Sea butterflies. It grabs the shell, hooks the soft body, and pulls it out whole.
But sea butterflies vanish for much of the year. So how does it not starve?
It burns its own fat. In a lab, one survived about 356 days with nothing.
It shrank from 22 millimeters to 12, but it was still swimming. Almost a year, no meal.

description:
A sea angel survived about 356 days in a lab without a single meal.
These shell-less sea slugs of the Arctic eat almost only sea butterflies, hook them, and pull them out of their shells. When prey vanishes, they live off stored fat, shrinking from about 22 to 12 millimeters while still swimming.
Could you go a whole year on your own reserves? Comment below.
first_comment: Sea angels are Arctic sea slugs with no shell, and some reach 7 to 8 centimeters. Would you rank them as cute or creepy?
